tasks.title: usage: gauge total under a millisecond tie
tasks.note: DatabaseTest "addBatch gauge" writes two gauge rows stamped with the current time to the millisecond, then reads the newest. When both land in the same millisecond, which one wins depends on the tie-break order; PHP returned 100 and Rust 200 in one CI run, after passing in every earlier one. Check that the database tie-break on equal times matches PHP.

tasks.title: Database: known gaps after 8.3.6
tasks.note: CollectionTests::testKeywords on postgres and mysql: PHP loses a metadata transaction under lane load (passes alone). Join aliases: main relaxed PHP's alias rule (leading digits, hyphens) after the freeze, and CI runs PHP merged with main. Vector $distance: CI's pgvector returns fewer digits than the recording machine; PHP and Rust agree. The DateTime::formatTz fuzz differs by milliseconds of wall time. Memory testDeleteBulkDocuments is timing-dependent. SQL.php line numbers: main moved PHP to database 8.3.8, so TypeError messages quote lines 4234 and 5821 where the frozen 8.3.6 recordings and Rust say 4213 and 5779; the errors themselves match.

tasks.title: Callbacks as async closures, without Box::pin
tasks.note: utopia-http actions take async |scope| { .. } and platform callbacks take Callback::http, ::task and ::worker, so guides read like PHP's ->action(function () { .. }). A callback that cannot fail returns nothing; only one that uses ? ends with Ok(()). CONVERSION.md makes it the rule.

tasks.title: Adapter traits take async fn, without BoxFuture
tasks.note: Implementing a Transport, Client, Consumer or other adapter still means BoxFuture return types and Box::pin bodies (agents, abuse and domains guides show it). Move them to async fn with an object-safe companion trait, as utopia-cache's Adapter and DynAdapter do.
